column1: # Benchmark workloads, read by every runner so all of them do the same work.
# Input arrays are not stored here; they are generated from these parameters by
# a formula both runners implement (see benchmarks/README.md). Every runner
# reports a checksum of the arrays it generated, and compare.py refuses to
# compare runs whose checksums differ — otherwise a "faster" number could just
# fill_every  1 fills on every element; n fills on one element in n. The rest
#             are size-zero orders, which the kernel ignores without writing a
#             record. Fill rate matters more than it looks: at 100% the run is
#             memory-bound on record writing rather than compute-bound.
# price_mode  close     order price is this bar's close (+inf sentinel)
#             prev      the previous bar's close (-inf sentinel)
